text: . In Skating, India’s 16-year-old speed skater Anirudhan Vinod won gold in the junior men’s one-lap road race at the World Skate Games 2026 in Asunción, Paraguay, clocking 30.394 seconds.His compatriot Lohnath Arun Prasath secured silver in the event. The margin between the two skaters was just 0.025 seconds.

. Ukrainian forces launched one of their largest aerial assaults on Russia today, sending more than 1,000 drones across the country and setting an oil export terminal ablaze in St. Petersburg. Governor Alexander Beglov said one person was killed and five were injured in the attack, which sparked fires at both the Petersburg Oil Terminal and the city’s Ruchi oil depot.Russia’s Defence Ministry said that its forces had destroyed 1,015 Ukrainian drones over 15 Russian regions, as well as the Russian-controlled Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black Sea. Russian forces launched two attacks on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, killing a woman and injuring at least two other people.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned Russia’s continued aerial strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, accusing Moscow of violating an energy ceasefire announced by US President Donald Trump. In a social media post, Zelenskyy said Russia had carried out 76 attacks targeting Ukraine’s energy, oil and gas sectors in the week since Trump’s announcement, despite his call for both sides to halt such strikes.

. India’s Amruta Pujari has won a silver medal in the women’s 72-kilogram category at the Under-23 World Wrestling Championships in Las Vegas, United States. She lost to Ukraine’s Iryna Zablotska 0-6 in the gold-medal bout to finish second today.Earlier, Komal won a bronze medal in the women’s 59-kilogram category yesterday.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over  Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, Punjab, Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal for tomorrow. Similar weather conditions are expected over Andhra Pradesh and West Rajasthan.  IMD said that conditions are likely to become favourable for further withdrawal of southwest monsoon from some more parts of eastern India and many parts of northeast India during the next two days. Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Kerala can also experience thunderstorms accompanied with Lightning.

. President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to the countrymen on the occasion of Durga Puja today. In her message, the President said that the festival of Durga Puja reflects India’s rich spiritual heritage. She added that the festival of Durga Puja brings Indians together and the celebrations beautifully showcase India’s traditions, lifestyle, art and culture.President Murmu said that the victory of Goddess Durga over Mahishasura is an inspiring example of the triumph of divine forces over evil. She emphasised that Durga Puja reflects India’s tradition of revering the strength of women. The President said that people can express their true devotion to Goddess Durga by ensuring respect for women in every aspect of personal and social lives. She prayed that the blessings of Goddess Durga bring happiness and prosperity to all citizens and that the nation continues on the path of rapid development.

. India’s visually impaired judoka Kokila has assured herself of a medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya after defeating China’s Yi Liu 1-0 in the women’s J2 -52kg semifinal. She will face Kyrgyzstan’s Aibike Ulanbek Kyzy in the final later in the day, with gold at stake.Kokila, who won bronze in the -48kg category at the previous edition in Hangzhou, hails from Haryana’s Jind district and represented India at the Paris 2024 Paralympics.In the men’s J1 -70kg category, Kapil Parmar will compete for bronze after losing 0-1 to Indonesia’s Junaedi in the semifinal. He will face Indonesia’s Ahnaf Rafli Shidqi in the bronze medal playoff.

. Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav has informed that India’s Ramsar site tally has reached 103. In a social media post, the Minister said that India continues to strengthen its commitment to wetland conservation, with Sukhna Lake in Chandigarh and Sauj Jheel in Uttar Pradesh becoming the latest additions to the list of Ramsar Sites. Mr Yadav said that this milestone highlights the importance that Narendra Modi government has been laying on wetlands in conserving biodiversity, enhancing water and climate security, and sustaining local livelihoods. He said these additions reaffirm India’s ongoing efforts to conserve its rich wetland ecosystems and strengthen the ecological, climatic and livelihood benefits they provide. The Minister also congratulated Uttar Pradesh and Chandigarh for the achievement.

. In Asian markets today, South Korea’s Kospi surged over two per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 jumped 1.4 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose half a per cent, Taiwan’s Taiex added 0.3 per cent, and China’s Shanghai Composite as well as Singapore’s Strait Times gained over 0.2 per cent each.In European markets, Germany’s DAX soared one per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 added 0.1 per cent, when reports last came in.

. The AYUSH Ministry has issued standard treatment guidelines on Management of Dermatological Disorders for Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy, with the inclusion of Yoga. The document has been prepared by the Ayush Vertical of the Directorate General of Health Services and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The Ministry said that the document is intended to bring more uniformity, quality assurance and evidence-informed practice to clinical care across the Ayush systems. Ayush Minister Prataprao Jadhav underlined that these guidelines will deepen the integration of Ayush systems with the national healthcare framework. He said that by promoting standardised and evidence-informed clinical practice, the guiidelines will contribute to improving patient care and strengthening the role of Ayush systems in public health.

. In cricket, Indian men’s team will face the West Indies in the decisive fifth and final T20 International at M. Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru this evening. With the five-match series level at two-all. The game is scheduled to begin at 7 PM Indian Standard Time.India will now aim to extend their unbeaten streak in home T20I series, a run dating back to February 2019 when Australia last won a T20I series on Indian soil. A victory for the West Indies, however, would secure their first bilateral T20I series win in India, ending the hosts’ remarkable streak and marking their first series win against India across any format on Indian soil since 2003.Led by Shreyas Iyer, India have added veteran pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar to their squad, resting Jasprit Bumrah.India leads the West Indies 22-12 in their overall T20I head-to-head record, with one match ending in a no result.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal today. Heavy rainfall is also expected over Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe and South Interior Karnataka till tomorrow.The Met Department predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Telangana, Madhya Pradesh, Konkan, Goa and Maharashtra for the day. Similar weather conditions are also expected over Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands today. For Delhi, the Weather Agency has forecast a clear sky today.

. Bangladesh’s Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has filed a charge sheet against Saima Wazed, daughter of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, over allegations of submitting false information in her application for the post of Regional Director for South-East Asia at the World Health Organization (WHO).According to the investigation, Wazed allegedly claimed to have worked as an honorary specialist or expert at Bangladesh Medical University. Investigators alleged that the credentials were used to secure the WHO position and that pressure was exerted to forward supporting documents through official channels without proper verification. ACC Secretary disclosed this in a media briefing.The case was filed at the ACC’s Dhaka-1 Integrated District Office on March 20 last year. The charges invoke several provisions of Bangladesh’s Penal Code and the Prevention of Corruption Act. The allegations remain subject to judicial proceedings.

. Saudi Arabia says it has intercepted and destroyed four drones over Riyadh, the Eastern Province and southern regions, as Houthi attacks continue. In a separate incident, two crew members were killed when a reconnaissance helicopter crashed in the kingdom’s Najran region due to a technical malfunction, according to the Saudi-led coalition.Meanwhile, Egypt is preparing to discuss potential support for Saudi Arabia’s defences, with parliament set to hold an emergency session on Sunday after President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi sought authorisation to provide assistance if requested by Riyadh.In Yemen, Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for a missile attack on Aden International Airport on Friday. Two missiles landed within the airport complex, around 500 metres from a Yemenia Airways aircraft preparing to depart for Cairo. Yemen’s information minister said passengers and crew were safe.Separately, a tugboat travelling south near the UAE’s Khor Fakkan reported being struck by two unidentified projectiles, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency. The vessel sustained damage, and one person suffered minor injuries, but the tug continued on its route. An LNG tanker off Yemen’s Mukalla also reported coming under gunfire from people aboard a small skiff.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed grief over the loss of lives in a road accident in Gwalior. He conveyed his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured.Fifteen devotees were killed and 42 others injured in the accident. Union Minister for Communications Jyotiraditya Scindia visited the hospital on Sunday to enquire about the condition of the injured and directed officials to ensure the best possible treatment.Mr. Scindia called for a fair and stringent investigation into the accident and demanded action against those responsible. The district administration has ordered a magisterial inquiry and directed that the report be submitted within seven days. On the directions of Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav, a CSP has been removed from the post and eight police personnel have been suspended.The state government has announced financial assistance of four lakh rupees each to the families of the deceased, two lakh rupees each to those seriously injured, and 50,000 rupees each to other injured persons. Meanwhile, the Prime Minister has announced an ex-gratia payment of two lakh rupees from the Prime Minister’s National Relief Fund to the next of kin of each person who lost their life in the accident, and 50,000 rupees each to the injured.

. The Indian Embassy in Riyadh has advised the Indian community in Saudi Arabia to take due precautions under the prevailing situation and immediately proceed to the nearest safe place in case of an aerial attack. In an advisory issued today, the Embassy urged them to refrain from filming, publishing, or sharing any information, photos, or videos related to the ongoing events. The Embassy officials continue to visit hospitals where injured Indian nationals are receiving medical treatment, and are in constant touch with their family and providing necessary assistance.Meanwhile, Riyadh’s international airport remains closed to flight operations. Dammam, Jeddah, and Medina airports remain operational, although some disruptions continue. Indian carriers have extended the suspension of flights to and from Saudi Arabia. Air India, Air India Express, and Indigo have extended suspension of flights until 24th October on all routes. Akasa Air has suspended its flights until 27h October on all routes.The Embassy said Saudia Airlines continues to operate scheduled flights to Indian destinations from Dammam, Jeddah and Medina. It asked Indian nationals requiring urgent departure to consider transiting via Bahrain, Kuwait, or Qatar, subject to obtaining the necessary visas. Indian nationals planning to travel to Saudi Arabia, including for Umrah, have been advised to take into account ongoing disruptions at Saudi airports and possibility of flight cancellations, which may result in extended stays.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar will meet the Foreign Minister of the UAE, Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, in Mumbai today. Earlier, briefing the media in New Delhi, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the visit of the UAE Foreign Minister will be an opportunity to review all facets of bilateral cooperation under the India-UAE Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The two sides will assess and take forward initiatives in the areas of energy, trade and investments, fintech, defence and connectivity.The spokesperson said the External Affairs Minister will also hold talks with the US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, tomorrow in Mumbai. Dr Jaishankar will attend the celebration of the 250th Anniversary of the Independence of the US as the guest of honour. Mr Jaiswal said the forthcoming visit of the US Secretary of State will provide an opportunity for both sides to review India-US relations and discuss ways to further strengthen the Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership.He further stated that discussions are expected to cover key areas of bilateral cooperation, including energy, trade and investment, Defence, critical and emerging technologies, and other areas of mutual interest. The two sides will also exchange views on regional and global developments. The visit will provide an opportunity to sustain the high-level engagement between the two countries and advance their shared priorities.

. The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways has said that cargo movement on inland waterways increased from 29 million metric tonnes in 2014-15 to 218 million metric tonnes in 2025-26, registering a compound annual growth rate of 20.13 per cent. The Ministry said the growth has already surpassed the target of 200 million metric tonnes set under Maritime India Vision 2030. India has 111 National Waterways, extending over 20,187 kilometres across 23 states and four Union Territories. The Ministry added that the country is strengthening its inland waterway network through hydrographic surveys, modern navigation infrastructure and digital information systems to support the growing movement of cargo on rivers..

. The Mahaashtami-related puja and other rituals started early this morning. Necessary security arrangements and crowd management systems are in place after the stampede incident in Kolkata on Saturday last week. 10 days police custody has been ordered by the bankshal court in Kolkata for the seven accused in the incident yesterday.Today is Mahaashtami. The Mahaashtami puja and rituals like anjali have started early this morning. Necessary preparations are underway for Sandhi Puja across all puja mandaps, including Belur Math. Kumari Puja is a special ritual at Belur Math, and it will be performed today on the occasion of Mahaashtami. In addition to Belur Math, Kumari Puja is also being performed at other Ramakrishna Math and Mission branches across West Bengal, as well as at a few other Hindu maths in the state. The state government has taken necessary measures for crowd management in all puja pandals across West Bengal in the aftermath of the Chorbagan stampede incident that took place last week in Kolkata.

. Kenya’s Charles Matata broke the course record to win the men’s elite race at the Vedanta Delhi Half Marathon today, while Ethiopia’s Wudinesh Alemu claimed the women’s title. Matata clocked 58 minutes, 52 seconds over the 21.097-kilometre course, shaving one second off the previous record set by Ethiopia’s Amedework Walelegn in 2020.Matata set the record to earn an additional 12,000 dollars on top of the 27,000 dollar winner’s prize. Kenya swept the men’s podium, with Samwel Nyamai Mailu finishing second in 59 minutes, 24 seconds and Stanley Waithaka Mburu third in 59 minutes, 33 seconds.Alemu won the women’s race in 1 hour, 6 minutes, 35 seconds. Kenya’s Selah Businei finished second in 1 hour, 7 minutes, 1 second, followed by Cynthia Chelangat Chepkwony in 1 hour, 7 minutes, 32 seconds.In the Indian elite men’s race, Shailesh Kushwaha won in one hour, five minutes and five seconds, ahead of Gaurav Mathur in one hour, five minutes and 11 seconds, and Hemant Kumar in one hour, five minutes and 37 seconds.Ankita Dhyani won the Indian elite women’s title in one hour, 12 minutes and 46 seconds. Soniya finished second in one hour, 14 minutes and 56 seconds, while Bhagirathi was third in one hour, 15 minutes and 51 seconds.Union Minister Kiren Rijiju, Chief of Defence Staff Gen. N.S. Raja Subramani and World Athletics Vice President Adille Sumariwalla attended the event. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta flagged off the Great Delhi Run.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah is visiting Punjab tomorrow to share the pain of those bereaved families whose members have recently been killed for raising their voices against drug traffickers in the state. In a social media post, Mr Shah blamed the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government for the prevailing drug menace in Punjab, which has caused many families to lose their sons. He will be meeting the families of those who recently lost their lives in Mansa, Gurdaspur and Sangrur districts, when they raised their voices against the ‘chitta’ (synthetic drug) traffickers, who have allegedly been flourishing under the patronage of the AAP government.He said the grief these families are enduring is beyond words and any attempt to silence those who speak out against drugs will never succeed. Mr Shah said the Government of India will systematically track down these drug traffickers and put them behind bars, ensuring that Punjab and the entire nation- gets rid of the the drug menace.

. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has extended the submission deadline for Stage II of the Viksit Bharat Essay Challenge to 22nd of this month. The Ministry said that the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) 2027, has received an overwhelming response from across the country. It informed that over 1.45 crore attempts have been recorded in the Viksit Bharat Quiz as part of the selection process. The Ministry added that about 5.7 lakh youth who qualified in the Quiz round have moved to the next stage, the Viksit Bharat Essay Challenge, where they must submit a 500-word essay on the MY Bharat portal on the theme designated for their region.The Ministry further advised the youth who have not yet submitted their essays to submit them by the 22nd of this month. It said that the extension gives eligible participants more time to submit their essays and encourages wider participation in this national initiative.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has revised the timings and operational framework of the Closing Auction Session in the equity cash market. It has also updated the settlement methodology for stock and index derivatives contracts. Under the new framework, the Closing Auction Session will operate for 10 minutes, from 3.30 PM to 3.40 PM, on all trading days. The session will include different phases for calculating the reference price and placing orders. The order-entry window will close randomly between 3.38 PM and 3.40 PM.Trading in stock and index derivatives will continue until 3.45 PM. On expiry days, however, trading in expiring index derivatives contracts will end at 3.30 PM. Stock derivatives trading will continue until 3.45 PM. The post-closing session in the cash market will run from 3.50 PM to 4 PM, with trades executed at the closing price.SEBI has also revised the method for calculating settlement prices on expiry days. For index derivatives, settlement prices will be based on the underlying index value, calculated using the volume-weighted average prices of constituent stocks during the final 30 minutes of continuous trading. For stock derivatives, settlement prices will be based on the volume-weighted average price of the underlying stock during the same period.The regulator has also specified rules for carrying forward unexecuted orders into the Closing Auction Session. These include provisions for iceberg orders, which will be converted into fully disclosed limit orders, subject to specified conditions. The revised provisions, except those relating to the transition of unexecuted orders, will take effect from 7 December 2026. The provisions concerning unexecuted limit and iceberg orders will come into force on 8 February 2027. SEBI has directed stock exchanges and clearing corporations to make the necessary system and procedural changes in consultation with the regulator within seven days of its circular issued yesterday.

. The Asian Para Games 2026 began today in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with India aiming to build on its record medal haul at the previous edition. The fifth edition of the continental sporting event will run until October 24, featuring competitions across 18 sports. The opening ceremony was held at Paloma Mizuho Stadium in Nagoya under the theme, “WABI: We Are Beautiful Individuals”. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi welcomed athletes and officials from across Asia.India is targeting a 100-medal haul, with para-athletics head coach Satyanarayana expressing confidence in the contingent’s preparation, determination and ability to deliver a strong performance. At the 2023 edition in Hangzhou, China, India achieved a historic milestone by winning a record 111 medals.Para-badminton player Pramod Bhagat and sprinter Simran Sharma are leading the Indian contingent as flag-bearers. India has sent a 281-member contingent, including 168 athletes and 113 officials and support staff. The athletes, comprising 112 men and 56 women, will compete in 11 disciplines. The Indian squad includes prominent para-athletes such as javelin thrower Sumit Antil, shooter Avani Lekhara, archer Sheetal Devi, sprinter Simran Sharma, Pramod Bhagat and Bhavina Patel.The event will be streamed live on the Waves OTT app and Prasar Bharati Sports’ YouTube channel.

. Media accreditation for the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 has been extended by two days. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting today said that media professionals planning to cover the festival can submit their applications through the official Press Information Bureau (PIB) accreditation portal till the 17th of this month. The Ministry advised eligible media persons to complete their registration and upload the required documents before the revised deadline.The 57th edition of IFFI 2026 will be held from 20th to 28th of next month, in Panaji, Goa.

. Iran’s newly appointed Defence Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi has warned US President Donald Trump against launching further attacks on Iran, asserting that Tehran has taken all necessary measures to counter the “Mother of All Bombs” and is confident in its military preparedness.Akhlaghi’s remarks came after Iran’s Parliament approved his appointment as Minister of Defence and Armed Forces Logistics today, with 237 lawmakers voting in favour and 15 against his nomination, out of 277 votes cast. Addressing Parliament ahead of the vote, Akhlaghi warned that Iran would deliver a strong response if its adversaries launched another attack against the country. He warned Trump against further escalation, urging him to focus on the safe withdrawal of US forces from the region and cautioning that any further threats would carry consequences. Akhlaghi succeeded Aziz Nasirzadeh, who was killed in US-Israeli attacks on Tehran, following which Pezeshkian appointed Brigadier General Seyyed Majid Ibn al-Reza as acting defence minister.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will visit Dushanbe in Tajikistan to represent India at the 25th Meeting of the Council of Heads of Government of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). The two-day meeting will start from today.The Defence Ministry said that the meeting will focus on strengthening multilateral cooperation among SCO Member States, particularly in the areas of trade, economy, investment, connectivity, innovation and cultural-humanitarian exchanges. It added that the meeting is expected to review the progress of ongoing cooperation initiatives and consider decisions regarding the Organisation’s financial and institutional functioning.The meeting will also provide an opportunity for India to exchange views with other SCO Member States on advancing practical and mutually beneficial cooperation within the Organisation. India remains actively engaged in various SCO mechanisms and continues to contribute to regional cooperation through initiatives in areas such as start-ups and innovation, digital public infrastructure, and people-to-people exchanges.

. Recovering well at Zayed Military Hospital in Abu Dhabi, Captain Smit Machchhar has given a detailed account of what he recalls from the day of the incident aboard flydubai flight FZ1073. In interviews with The National and Sky News Arabia, published on 17th October, Captain Smit recounted how he was attacked by his co-pilot on the Dubai to Tel Aviv flight on 30th September. He has described the repeated blows, his attempts to get help, the cockpit door opening and shutting, and how he repeatedly lost consciousness as he fought to survive.Just before the attack, the other captain travelling as deadweight crew and who Captain Smit has described as a good friend, came into the cockpit and the two discussed their roasters, schedules, etc. Around this time, the co-pilot wanted to take a toilet break even as the two captains continued their conversation. A few minutes into the conversation, the co-pilot said he wanted to pray. Accordingly, the other captain stepped out of the cockpit and the co-pilot started praying, positioned just behind Captain Smit.Captain Smit was seated, checking routine information like expected landing time on his computer, “And that’s when it started,” he said. He suddenly felt a very hard hit at the back of his head. The impact was so hard that he fell forward, almost falling on his control column and he thought there was something catastrophically wrong with the aircraft structure. But in the next couple of seconds, as the hits kept coming, he managed to glance back and realised what was going on. The person hitting him was his colleague in the cockpit, that he thought was supposed to be part of the team.Captain Smit said that his vision had become very narrow because of the blows, restricted to just a few inches and he could only see outlines. His immediate reaction was to guard himself from further hits. He quickly unbuckled his seatbelt, turned around and tried to block the blows. “And that’s when something flipped and I said, okay, I need to get some help in here,” he recalled. Captain Smit started screaming the other Captain’s name, tried to reach the switch to open the cockpit door and get help. Amid the screaming and everything going on, he lost consciousness for the first time, he said.He remembers being able to open the door, there was some shouting between the other captain and the co-pilot, and the door shut immediately after this. Barely staying conscious, Captain Smit heard the engine sounds going down and he felt the aircraft going into a dive. Having flown for a long time, Captain Smit said, he did not need the instruments to understand that the engines were spooling down and the aircraft was going down.Throughout this time, he was in and out of consciousness, he recalled. Smit said his memories of what happened next are still fragmented. But he remembers trying to reach the cockpit door. The next thing he remembers is lying face down between the cockpit and the galley, with the cockpit door open. He recalled a scene of panic, screaming and chaos. Several people were trying to control the situation in the cramped space around the cockpit entrance.Captain Smit said he was eventually pulled out of the cockpit and the senior cabin crew member reached him and helped him. Looking back, Smit said there was a moment when he thought he might not survive. “I told myself that, Smith, do something. You can’t die like this,” he said. He had not accepted his death, but realised he had to do something or he might not survive.It was the first time Captain Smit had met the co-pilot, and he said their interaction before the attack was usual and normal. He said there was nothing in their interaction that made him suspect anything was wrong. “It was the first time we met… there were some small talks… But nowhere till the point that anything would have caused me to think that, ‘Hey, hold on, there’s something off.’” Captain Smit also added that flying with new crew members was a routine part of the job and that the flight had started like any other, with no uncertainty about the journey.Captain Smit acknowledged the role played by his crew during the incident, describing them as his “very, very, very efficient crew who saved my life”. He also praised the other captain who took over the controls of the aircraft in an emergency. “The other thing, how my other colleague took over the controls and saved the day again is commendable. It’s something that I’ll keep with me till I die.” He also thanked the passengers saying “everyone did their best” and expressed gratitude to people wishing him for his recovery from across the world.Captain Smit also expressed gratitude to the UAE government for the medical care and support he received following the incident. “The medical care which I was given and the sheer support of the entire UAE government I will never forget in my life.”On being asked about the source of his courage to face such odds, he said he valued mental power & mental preparedness; and in that moment, it was like survival instinct kicked in for him and all the others onboard, on the day it mattered.Captain Smit looked in good health in the interview, smiling and articulating well. Speaking from his hospital bed, he said the experienced medical team had brought him to a stage where his care could now be handed over to his family. Looking ahead, he expressed optimism about returning to work soon, saying he could not wait to put on his uniform and get back to flying, “I will be back in action hopefully soon. And I can’t wait to put on the uniform and get back to work”. Despite the traumatic experience, Smit said his love for aviation remained unchanged, “Did my love die for aviation? Not at all. Not at all.”

. Domestic investors are set to navigate a week packed with key market drivers, including macroeconomic data, corporate earnings results, and geopolitical developments. Market sentiment will also be driven by foreign institutional investor (FII) flows, commodity prices, bond yield movements, and currency fluctuations during the holiday-shortened week ahead.Indian equity markets will remain closed on Tuesday on account of Dussehra. Market participants will closely track the country’s core industries growth figures and forex reserves data. On the primary market front, two mainboard IPOs are set to open for subscription, including one of the biggest IPOs in India so far.Globally, investors will closely monitor developments surrounding the West Asia conflict. Bank of South Korea is scheduled to declare its monetary policy decision. In Japan, inflation data will be on focus along with an eye on China’s third quarter GDP estimates and industrial production data.

. Today is World Cotton Day. This day is celebrated annually on October 7 to highlight the global economic, social, and environmental importance of cotton. The theme for this year is Cotton for Good: Building Prosperity Through Trade, Transformation and Partnership. Sharing a video message, Union Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh extended greetings to everyone associated with this sector.He said that this day honours farmers who cultivate cotton in the fields, thereby enabling employment for workers across the entire value chain, whether in spinning mills, ginneries, textile manufacturing units, or garment factories. He informed that 60 lakh farmers in the country are engaged in cotton cultivation. He underlined that countless small enterprises are linked to the handloom industries that not only operate domestically but also export their products.

. A white paper, released by the Confederation of Indian Industry – CII, has said that India needs to accelerate growth in its media and entertainment sector to roughly 15 percent annually, to reach its 100 billion dollar ambition by the early 2030s. With the current 9 percent annual growth rate, the sector would reach only about 64 billion dollars by 2033, leaving a revenue gap of USD 36 billion.Released at the CII Big Picture Summit 2026 in Mumbai today, the white paper titled ‘The New Economics of Media & Entertainment’, lists market-led broadcasting, measurable action against piracy, and investment in regional markets and emerging businesses as immediate priorities to achieve the goal.Speaking on the occasion, Summit Chair and MD & CEO, Sony Pictures Networks,  Gaurav Banerjee said India has achieved audience scale; the next imperative is to create, capture and retain greater value from it. He added that CII is seeking greater freedom over television pricing and packaging, removal of carriage fees, restored audience measurement, and transparent standards across screens. It has further proposed reducing GST on television, OTT and music subscriptions to 5 percent, alongside proportionate regulation and industry self-regulation.The paper states that the next phase of growth will come from new technologies and business models, including responsible AI, virtual production, connected TV and creator-led formats and from industries beyond entertainment that need Indian studios’ animation, gaming, XR and digital-mapping skills.Considering that India has about 6.8 cinema screens per million people with Bihar and Uttar Pradesh having the lowest screen densities, CII has proposed setting up over 16 thousand screens by early 2030 while promoting regional-language content, connectivity and local creative talent.<>
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 0.3 per cent up at 1,46,426 rupees per 10 grams. Silver surged over 1.2 per cent to 2,10,918 rupees per kilogram.

. Indian Air Force (IAF) aircraft C-130J undertook a short-notice casualty evacuation from Leh to Palam. The Defence Ministry said that the aircraft airlifted a critically ill civilian patient for further medical care. The mission was carried out in darkness and challenging weather conditions, requiring a high degree of operational preparedness, professional coordination and timely execution. The Ministry said that the mission reflects IAF’s operational readiness and its ability to respond promptly to critical humanitarian requirements, including medical evacuation under challenging conditions.

. French President Emmanuel Macron has vowed legal action against those responsible for violence during protests across the country and described it as an attempt to bring ‘down the republic’. In a televised address to the nation yesterday, Macron said those responsible for vandalism and looting would be held accountable. He also stressed the importance of distinguishing between protesters with legitimate grievances and those involved in violent incidents.According to France’s Interior Ministry, nearly two thousand four hundred people were arrested on Saturday, while around one thousand police officers and gendarmes were injured during the unrest. Several government buildings, shops and public properties were damaged, with incidents reported in multiple cities. Macron said the government would review the events and take appropriate steps to prevent similar incidents in the future.He emphasised the importance of restoring public order while ensuring the safety of residents and local communities affected by the unrest. The president also acknowledged the challenges faced by people whose businesses, homes and neighbourhoods had been affected. He announced plans to establish a crisis unit to coordinate urgent assistance for those impacted by the violence and help communities recover from the damage.

The Digital India BHASHINI Division and the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, have developed text-to-speech (TTS) models for Sourashtra, a minority Indo-Aryan language spoken predominantly by the Sourashtra community in Tamil Nadu. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology said the initiative aims to expand the availability of speech technology for languages with limited digital resources. It will also support the use of these languages in digital applications, language learning, accessibility solutions, documentation, and research. According to the Ministry, the newly developed models use a Variational Inference with Adversarial Learning-based end-to-end text-to-speech architecture, enabling them to generate Sourashtra speech directly from text. The models feature both male and female voices, with each voice supporting text written in both Tamil and Sourashtra scripts. This enables users to access and use Sourashtra in the scripts commonly used to write the language.

Chasing 103 runs, India comfortably reached the target in just 8.5 overs for the loss of one wic. Earlier, opting to bat first, Zimbabwe posted 102 for 8 in their allotted 20 overs. Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano top-scored with 34 runs off 32 balls. . Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Located at Teen Murti Marg in New Delhi, the Pradhanmantri Sangrahalaya inspires the younger generation by showcasing the vision, leadership and contributions of all the Prime Ministers.Pradhanmantri Sangrahalaya, inaugurated by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2022, highlights the contributions of all the Prime Ministers to the nation’s development. The museum showcases how Indian democracy has provided opportunities for leaders from every section of society to contribute to nation-building. Spread across two buildings, the modern digital museum offers visitors an insight into India’s political history, democratic traditions and journey of development. The Sangrahalaya features a Light and Sound Show titled ‘Veeranganaon ki Mahagatha’, which narrates the inspiring stories of valiant women warriors who fought to uphold the nation’s pride. Inaugurating the Pradhanmantri Sangrahalaya, Prime Minister Modi described the museum as a living symbol of the shared heritage and collective contributions of all governments.During his visit to the Pradhanmantri Sangrahalaya, Justice S. Thurairaja of Sri Lanka shared his reflections on India’s democratic journey and the leadership that has shaped the nation.

In France, Police arrested at least 1,800 people across the country after violent groups clashed with officers and looted shops during nationwide demonstrations that drew hundreds of thousands of people who denounced rising living costs and poor conditions in schools. Authorities said masked groups yesterday set fires and attacked public buildings, including city halls, in several cities.In Limoges, a city in central France, flames engulfed the 19th-century City Hall, causing its roof to collapse. In the southern port city of Marseille, some protesters briefly forced their way into the lobby of City Hall, and a police station was damaged. In Lyon, a fire broke out inside a tourist office. Authorities said about 550,000 people took part in protests across France. Paris police in a statement said, One person died of a heart attack, without providing further details. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said More than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters were injured. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, saying peaceful protests were acceptable but arson, looting and attacks were not. French President Emmanuel Macron will hold an emergency meeting with top government officials today, before addressing the nation this evening.

Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across Belgium, France, Italy and Portugal to protest against rising living costs, low wages and the growing difficulty of accessing affordable housing. The demonstrations have put governments across the European Union under pressure.France witnessed widespread unrest, with more than five lakh fifty thousand people participating in demonstrations, according to the Interior Ministry. The protests, which followed weeks of student demonstrations, escalated into clashes, widespread looting and arson as groups of masked protesters targeted shops, historic public buildings and police vehicles.French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said around 1,200 people had been arrested and 150 police officers injured. Dozens of shops were looted in several cities, including Paris, Marseille, Nice, Bordeaux and Toulouse.In Limoges, a fire set by masked protesters largely destroyed the historic town hall. Municipal buildings in Marseille and Lille were vandalised, while a tourist office in Lyon was set ablaze. French President Emmanuel Macron vowed that those responsible would be prosecuted.In Belgium, police used tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in Brussels and Liège following reports of projectiles being thrown at officers and fires being set.Meanwhile, tens of thousands of people reportedly marched in Portugal’s capital, Lisbon, protesting against rising living costs, low wages and soaring housing prices. Portuguese Parliamentary Affairs Minister Carlos Abreu Amorim said the government would not yield to pressure from street demonstrations, while protesters accused political leaders of being out of touch with their concerns.In Italy, demonstrations in Milan against wars and rising living costs turned violent, with protesters clashing with police, looting shops and setting fire to barricades. Police used tear gas and water cannon to disperse the crowds. According to the LaPresse news agency, at least two police officers were injured and around 50 demonstrators were detained.Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned the violence, saying that while demonstrating was a right, setting cities ablaze was unacceptable. Milan Mayor Giuseppe Sala also said that although the protesters’ concerns were understandable, violence against police and damage to public property could not be justified. Clashes were also reported in Bologna, where some demonstrators allegedly threw stones at police.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today met Governor of the Japan Bank for International Cooperation, Kazuhiko Amakawa, on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok. The two sides discussed expanding cooperation in clean energy, semiconductors and critical minerals. In a social media post, Finance Ministry said, the discussions focused on strengthening cooperation in energy transition, advanced manufacturing, electric mobility and resilient supply chains. They also explored cooperation through the 600-million-dollar India-Japan Fund and Japanese participation in the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund.During the meeting, Ms Sitharaman encouraged Japanese investors to explore opportunities in data centres in Tier Two and Tier Three cities, including Visakhapatnam. She said such investments could help promote more balanced urban development.Mr Amakawa highlighted the success of the India-Japan Fund in electric mobility and bioethanol. He also expressed hope for a follow-on fund and noted growing Japanese interest in semiconductors, artificial intelligence and data centres.The Finance Minister is on a five-day official visit to Bangkok in Thailand, till 18th of this month to attend the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings.

. Durga Puja is being celebrated with religious fervour and traditional enthusiasm across Odisha today, with beautifully decorated pandals and temples drawing large numbers of devotees. Special rituals are being performed at Shakti Peethas, while major cities, including Bhubaneswar and Cuttack, are witnessing festive gatherings and elaborate decorations. The celebrations reflect Odisha’s rich cultural heritage and the enduring significance of Goddess Durga as the symbol of divine power and the triumph of good over evil.Tripura is immersed in the festive spirit of Durga Puja, with celebrations underway across the state. Devotees and visitors are thronging puja pandals to offer prayers and seek the blessings of Goddess Durga. Colourful illuminations, beautifully decorated pandals and festive activities have created a vibrant atmosphere in various localities.In a resounding testament to cultural heritage and communal unity, the Bengali-speaking Barak Valley of Assam has immersed itself in the grand celebrations of Durga Puja.Beyond its religious significance, Durga Puja in Barak Valley stands out as a unique symbol of interfaith harmony. In a beautiful confluence of cultures, members of both the Hindu and Muslim communities actively join hands during the festivities. From Muslim artisans contributing to the intricate pandal artwork and light setups to local volunteers helping manage crowds and welcoming visitors, the festival transcends religious boundaries to become a shared socio-cultural extravaganza for the entire valley.

The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has capped trade margins on 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs at 30 percent of their maximum retail price, a move expected to reduce MRPs by up to 70 per cent, depending on existing price structures. Under a Gazette notification issued on October 17, the revised prices will take effect on November 9. The intervention aims to curb excessive distribution and retail margins and ease the financial burden of cancer treatment.The drugs covered include immunotherapies used to treat more than 20 types of cancer, denosumab used by breast and prostate cancer patients, pegfilgrastim used to prevent neutropenia in cancer patients, and bevacizumab, approved for treating colon, ovarian and cervical cancers. Widely used medicines such as pembrolizumab, durvalumab and osimertinib are also covered, with the revised pricing expected to improve patient access. The decision builds on NPPA’s 2019 pilot trade margin rationalisation exercise, which capped margins on 42 anti-cancer drugs at 30 percent That intervention reduced the MRPs of 526 brands of non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines by up to 90 percent.The expanded list was recommended by an expert committee under the Directorate General of Health Services, comprising oncologists, medical specialists, hospital experts and government officials. The list will be updated periodically. NPPA imposed the cap under Paragraph 19 of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013. Manufacturers must inform the authority of revised prices within seven days of publication of the notification. They must also publish price lists on their websites and circulate them widely to retailers and hospitals.

. The country’s foreign exchange reserves declined over 8.5 billion US dollars (USD) to 726 billion US dollars during the week ended 9th of October. According to Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, dropped by 7.1 billion dollars to 597.6 billion dollars during the week. Gold reserves dropped by 1.3 billion dollars to 105 billion dollars. Special Drawing Rights fell by 109 million dollars to 18.5 billion dollars. The country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund dipped 10 million dollars to 4.78 billion dollars.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has called for strengthening ties with India, Latin American nations and other countries, warning that a future US president could adopt a hostile approach towards Israel.Presenting his security doctrine yesterday, nine days ahead of Israel’s October 27 election, Netanyahu said Israel must use the remaining years of US President Donald Trump’s presidency to strengthen bilateral ties while building alternative international partnerships. Trump endorsed Netanyahu’s re-election bid earlier the same day.Netanyahu cited India as an important partner and pointed to potential political changes in Latin America, including Brazil, as opportunities to expand Israel’s network of allies. He stressed the need to develop capabilities that would make Israel valuable to countries worldwide.

. India’s Lokesh Subramani won the boys’ Under-17 title at the Malaysia Squash Junior Open, beating local challenger Muhammad Ifwat Zulkifli in straight games in the final in Kuala Lumpur today. Lokesh, seeded second, defeated his opponent 11-6, 11-2, 11-8.Aadya Budhia and Aryaman Singh reached the semifinals in the Under-17 girls’ and boys’ categories, while Divyanshi Jain in Under-13 girls category, Avisha Agarwal in the Under-11 girls’ category, and Shravin Jain in Under-19 boys category made it to the quarterfinals.

. In the forex market, the rupee appreciated by nine paise to close at 94.96 rupees against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 101.66 in intra-day trade.

. Visually impaired footballer Marbom Boje from Arunachal Pradesh is representing India as part of the Indian Para football team at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. Boje is supported under the Chief Minister’s Athlete Coaching and Empowerment Scheme (CM ACES). The Asian Para Games 2026 will officially start from the 18th to the 24th of October, though some competitions are scheduled to take place days before the official ceremony.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over coastal and South Interior Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry for the next 2-3 days. The IMD said thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds may prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttarakhand, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura tomorrow. Meanwhile, Konkan and Goa may experience Hot and Humid weather tomorrow.
